In Zomba District in September 2024, most facilities, particularly rural government clinics, kept no out-patient files, so the paper Health Passport was the only medical record for most people.

Last twelve months. In April 2026 the link between the iCHIS community module for non-communicable diseases and MaHIS at health facilities was being finalised.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Mahis was under pilot at selected health centres nationwide on 3 September 2026. In 2025 the ministry piloted linking the National ID to electronic medical record systems in five health facilities in Karonga District.

Not held. The number of health centres in the pilot is not given, and no hospital beyond Queen Elizabeth Central is named as using the system. Nothing held shows a record retrieved at a second facility, or the community system's link in use.

NAM.short: An electronic system is fully in place at only two hospitals; most hospitals and clinics keep paper records (2025 study).
NAM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and Social Services launched its Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS) in Windhoek in 2011, and its own IT department supports the ministry's information systems. Managers interviewed for a study published in March 2026 said the ministry has developed an e-Health Strategy, cited as the National eHealth Strategy 2021-2025, to guide a digital platform for capturing patient data. The minister's budget speech of 6 May 2025 asked N$62.5 million for health data and policy support, with expanding the e-Health network among its priorities, and Namibia launched a National Digital Health Policy for 2026 to 2036 in February 2026.

Tiers in use. IHCIMS, launched for every facility, was fully deployed only at Windhoek Central Hospital and Oshakati State Hospital, on the study of September 2025.

Where data is digitised. Practitioners reach a patient's record only through the paper health passport and manual records, and there is no unique patient identifier, the same study states. The minister said in March 2026 that the system still faces paper-based records.

Last twelve months. The managers said in the study of March 2026 that the platform was starting with a billing module on pilot at Katutura and Windhoek Central hospitals.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The health minister said on 6 May 2025 that five health centres and 18 clinics had the e-Health system's network in operation. The study of September 2025 states that the ministry still relies on paper records in most hospitals and clinics.

Not held. No count or share of primary clinics keeping an electronic record is held: the five health centres and 18 clinics of May 2025 are sites with the network in place. No budget line names the record system itself.

NER.short: Computerised patient records were set up in health centres and district hospitals in three districts (November 2024); how many centres is not known.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The mid-term evaluation for Enabel, of November 2024, states that the Enabel project PASS Sutura started the digitalisation with recruited consultancy firms, with the Ministry of Health's digital health directorate involved. PASS Sutura is a Belgian bilateral project with EUR 14.5 million for health over 2022-2026, and a Netherlands co-financing of EUR 3.2 million to 31 March 2025 puts particular emphasis on digitalisation. On 8 July 2026 the health minister opened the workshop validating the costed roadmap of the Schéma Directeur National de la e-Santé 2025-2029.

Tiers in use. By November 2024 the project had set up digitalisation, including computerised medical records and billing, in the integrated health centres (CSI) and district hospitals of Dioundiou, Gothèye and Gaya.

Where data is digitised. Enabel states that a hospital information system built around a computerised medical record was put in place at the district hospitals of Gaya and Gothèye after field missions in February and April 2024.

Last twelve months. At the workshop of 8 July 2026 the Directorate of e-Santé presented OpenClinic, its project for a hospital information system and computerised patient record, as already under way.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The evaluation of November 2024 places the digitalised health centres in the project's three target health districts only. In September 2018 the ministry's strategy reported electronic patient record activity in two health districts, Gaya and Gothèye, of 72.

Not held. No count of health centres using the computerised record is held, and no denominator. Nothing held says whether the record is made at the point of care or keyed afterwards, and no sites or counts are given for OpenClinic.

NGA.short: 100 of Lagos State's 326 primary clinics record care electronically as it happens (May 2025); there is no national figure.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare's Nigeria Digital Health Architecture of December 2025 sets interoperable electronic health record systems across all levels of care as its first pillar. In the memorandum signed with the United States on 19 December 2025, Nigeria commits to roll digital medical records out in 20% of facilities by 2026 and 100% by 2030, and the United States plans approximately US$28 million for an enhanced electronic medical record system over 2026-2030.

Tiers in use. The Minister of State for Health told the National Council on Health on 20 November 2025 that over 200 hospitals are integrated with electronic medical records systems. In Lagos State an EMR was in use in primary health care centres in May 2025.

Where data is digitised. In May 2025 the Lagos State Primary Health Care Board described its EMR as working "at the point of care". The federal architecture of December 2025 states that health data systems remain largely siloed and paper based, especially in public facilities.

Last twelve months. On 16 September 2026 the minister of state for health said the electronic medical record systems deployed in health facilities are fragmented and that minimum standards would be set and enforced.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Lagos State Ministry of Health reported on 22 May 2025 the EMR platform deployed in 100 of the state's 326 primary health care facilities.

Not held. No national share or count of primary clinics using an EMR is held; the figure is Lagos State's alone, and the over 200 hospitals have no denominator or tier. No shared record on a unique identifier is evidenced, and Nigeria's own commitment to data systems is not broken down to the EHR.

RWA.short: All 42 district hospitals used electronic patient records in 2023, and the national system reached most public facilities by 2026; shared records are not shown.
RWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Rwanda Biomedical Centre slides of April 2026 present eBuzima as the national system for all public health facilities, served from the Ministry of Health's own domain. In a memorandum signed on 5 December 2025 and running from April 2026 to December 2030, the government commits to expand national EMR systems across all health facilities. The United States plans to allocate US$6,806,292 over 2026 and 2027 to the e-Buzima rollout, and Rwanda commits to pay the ongoing licensing, cloud and hardware costs the United States does not.

Tiers in use. A survey of April and May 2023 found all 42 district hospitals using an electronic medical record system, 35 of them OpenMRS. King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, a referral hospital in Kigali, runs an Integrated Health Management Information System that gives each patient a single record, the Tony Blair Institute reported in July 2026.

Where data is digitised. The April 2026 slides describe eBuzima as centralised, web-based and synchronising records across public facilities.

Last twelve months. By 8 April 2026 eBuzima had been rolled out to the majority of public health facilities, with its HIV key-population and PrEP modules running in one Kigali pilot site.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Tom Frieden wrote in a piece published in September 2026 that eBuzima is in more than two thirds of health centres. The 2023 survey found 71 of 215 randomly sampled public health centres (33.0%) using an electronic medical record system.

Not held. No unique patient identifier and no record retrieved at another facility is established. No count of facilities using eBuzima is held, nor who enters the record at the health centres or where it is keyed.

SDN.short: A hospital system with electronic medical records was launched at two hospital sites on 11 May 2026; routine use is not yet shown.
SDN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications launched the hospital management system (HMS) on 11 May 2026 as their own programme, on the Sudan News Agency's report. ICTworks' directory, as of July 2026, lists the Sudan eHealth Strategy of the WHO Global Observatory's 2014 cycle as the operative digital health instrument and states that no replacement has been promulgated.

Tiers in use. Phase one of the HMS started on 11 May 2026 at two hospital sites, Al-Nao hospital in Khartoum state and the diagnostic centre of Gedaref hospital, ahead of gradual expansion to health institutions in other states.

Where data is digitised. An MSc thesis at Sudan University of Science and Technology, of March 2021, states that hospitals in Sudan had no electronic medical records and kept patients' health records on paper.

Last twelve months. A directive published on 30 March 2026 has the Prime Minister ordering hospital systems digitised within two weeks through a first pilot phase at Soba teaching hospital and Gedaref hospital. The HMS launched on 11 May 2026 includes an electronic patient record and an electronic medical record.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The first phase directed in March 2026 covers two hospitals only, with wider expansion left to a later phased plan. The thesis of March 2021 states that government clinics had no electronic medical record and depended wholly on paper records.

Not held. Whether the two sites are in routine use, the hospitals' level and where the record is entered are not established. No funding source is named for any system, and no sites or counts are held for SudaHealth, the Khartoum State platform.

SEN.short: The patient record runs only at pilot sites, in 1% of the 102 health centres (October 2025); health posts are not counted.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank, in a paper of January 2026, names the Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene as lead agency, deploying the electronic medical record. The ministry's sector policy letter of 25 March 2025 sets the generalisation of the computerised patient record under its Health System Digitalisation Programme 2023-2029. The record is a core activity of the US$46 million health component of the IDA-financed Senegal Digital Economy Acceleration Project.

Tiers in use. The health ministry states that the record, which it calls the Dossier Patient Informatisé, has been in use since November 2024 at the Thierno Birahim Ndao regional hospital in Kaffrine. We Are Tech Africa reported on 30 April 2025 a completed pilot at two hospitals, the Khadim Rassoul health centre and the HLM Fass health post.

Where data is digitised. At the Kaffrine hospital the patient is created in the system at registration and the doctor enters observations directly into it after the consultation, on the ministry's account, since November 2024.

Last twelve months. The World Bank records that a pilot of the record across 51 health centres had not started as of December 2025, delayed by disagreement between the health and digital ministries.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The World Bank's results framework gives 1 per cent of the 102 district-level health centres as using electronic medical records at 31 October 2025. An electronic record was available for 200,000 primary care patients at the same date.

Not held. Retrieval of a patient's record at another facility is not stated, and the 1 per cent counts health centres only, with health posts outside it. Nothing held says whether the 51-centre pilot began in 2026.

SLE.short: Electronic records run at one government hospital and one clinic (2026); a national system is not known to have been bought.
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. OpenMRS's case study of April 2026 describes the PIH EMR as Partners In Health's own OpenMRS distribution. The National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 commits the Government to roll out Electronic Medical Records to all medical facilities by 2030 and names a Ministry of Health directorate as lead. The Ministry's request for expressions of interest of 18 December 2025 states that a donor grant finances the initial phase.

Tiers in use. The case study states that Koidu Government Hospital, a referral centre, uses the PIH EMR and that the EMR has run at Wellbody Clinic since 2015. The Ministry reported on 11 October 2023 that it and Smart Systems Sierra Leone Ltd had launched an EMR pilot at Connaught Hospital in Freetown.

Where data is digitised. The case study states that the EMR at the Maternal Center of Excellence in Koidu is entered at the point of care, with retrospective entry also possible.

Last twelve months. The Maternal Center of Excellence opened on 14 February 2026 with the EMR covering all its inpatient wards. On 18 December 2025 the Ministry's project unit asked firms to express interest in deploying an OpenMRS-based EMR across 300 health facilities.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The case study of April 2026 names one clinic using the PIH EMR, Wellbody Clinic. The Compact of 6 December 2025 gives a baseline of 5 health facilities implementing the system, in a network it puts at about 1,463 public facilities.

Not held. What share of primary clinics keep patient records electronically is not held, nor the present state of the pilots at other primary facilities. The Compact's baseline of 5 facilities is undated, and the Ministry's national EMR is not shown procured.

SOM.short: Two electronic record systems run in over 40 facilities (April 2026) and 111 primary facilities (2025); their share of all clinics is unknown.
SOM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. By its own account the Ministry of Health developed RAAD as a national electronic health record for primary healthcare, implemented between 2023 and 2025. Its bulletin for July to September 2023 says the pilot was supported by the Government of Sweden through SPIDER. The Caafimaad+ Digitalized Data System (C+ DDS) is run by the CaafimaadPlus consortium of ten NGOs, in partnership with the Federal Ministry of Health, and funded by EU Humanitarian Aid, as the consortium stated in April 2026.

Tiers in use. The ministry's case study places RAAD in public primary healthcare facilities only, between 2023 and 2025.

Where data is digitised. RAAD captures clinical data as routine care documentation, in place of an average of 15 paper forms, on the ministry's case study of 2023 to 2025. The consortium said in April 2026 that C+ DDS replaces manual reports with real-time entry and makes a family's record available at any facility on the system.

Last twelve months. The consortium reports growth from a five-facility pilot in mid-2024 to over 40 facilities by April 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In April 2026 the consortium reported C+ DDS operational in over 40 facilities across 9 regions and more than 25 districts of South-Central Somalia. The ministry's case study reports RAAD deployed in 111 public primary healthcare facilities across six states between 2023 and 2025.

Not held. No count of all primary clinics is held to set either figure against, and the two systems' facilities are not shown to be separate. No plan naming an electronic medical record, no unique patient identifier and no tier for the C+ DDS facilities is held.

SSD.short: Only an HIV treatment register at five sites is held; nothing shows general patient records, electronic or paper, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: Not held. No electronic medical record in use is held, and no dated statement that patient records are on paper at every tier. The 22.4% of health facilities that the February 2025 assessment records with facility-wide electronic systems comes with no system named.

STP.short: A patient record was piloted at the central hospital and in one health area in 2022; whether it was extended is not known.
STP.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Health Development Plan 2023-2032, dated September 2022, sets a strategic axis on expanding what it calls the single clinical process to the whole national health system. The Joint SDG Fund programme's final report of 26 July 2022 states that the Single Process module for patient files was developed inside DHIS2, the Ministry of Health's main information software, and that rolling it out beyond the pilot will be done with funding from other donors.

Tiers in use. In September 2022 the plan placed the record in a pilot phase at the Ayres de Menezes central hospital and the Água Grande Health Area.

Where data is digitised. The report of July 2022 states that patient data is entered from reception through the nurses and doctors, each patient's file reached by a bar code sticker and scanner.

Last twelve months. The plan of September 2022 states that the pilot is to be evaluated before expansion to the whole national health system.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. At 26 July 2022 the Single Process had not been rolled out to other districts and still needed consolidating in the first pilot district, Água Grande. The plan states that computerised clinical records are to be introduced gradually through a pilot model of health centres and the central hospital.

Not held. Nothing is dated after September 2022: whether the pilot was evaluated, consolidated or extended beyond Água Grande is not established. The health area's facilities are not named and no count of facilities using the record is given.

SWZ.short: A shared electronic record runs in 73% of all health facilities (2026); it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
SWZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Data.FI described the Client Management Information System (CMIS) in April 2026 as an open-source, government-owned electronic medical record. The Ministry of Health's HMIS unit describes itself as custodian of the digital health systems, with its own in-country developers working on CMIS. Data.FI, a PEPFAR-funded USAID agreement, reported for the period ending March 2024 that it funds and carries out CMIS system development, security assessment and facility network support.

Tiers in use. Data.FI described CMIS in April 2026 as in use in the outpatient department of Piggs Peak Government Hospital and at local health clinics.

Where data is digitised. Data.FI said in April 2026 that clinicians open a client's full record on a unique ID number at their point of service, and that the record is available to clinicians at another clinic if the patient moves district.

Last twelve months. The HMIS unit reported in June 2026 that the integration of CMIS with eLMIS runs for ART medicines only and is ready for a facility-level pilot. In the first quarter of 2026 its developers completed training that produced automated, FHIR-aligned data flows from CMIS to DHIS2.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Data.FI said in April 2026 that CMIS is used in 73% of the country's health facilities, with 233 live sites. For the period ending March 2024 it reported CMIS in use at 75% (247 of 327) of healthcare facilities.

Not held. No current plan naming CMIS and no domestic budget line for it is held. The 73% is a share of all health facilities with no denominator given, and no count of primary clinics alone is held.

SYC.short: A ministry system that includes electronic medical records has run since the end of 2021 (reported January 2024); who uses it is not known.
SYC.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Seychelles Nation reports the health minister saying on 17 October 2023 that the Ministry of Health is investing in an Electronic Health Information System encompassing Electronic Medical Records, the ministry's name for it. The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 sets specific objective 6.8, "Implement eHIS", and names the Health Care Agency as lead entity, with the Ministry of Health and the Public Health Authority contributing.

Tiers in use. The minister said in October 2023 that the system is to be accessible to all health professionals throughout the health system.

Where data is digitised. At its digital health visioning meeting of 22 January 2024 the ministry said it was trying to link the system with laboratories and X-ray so that doctors get results on their computers.

Last twelve months. A ministry press release carried by Seychelles Nation in January 2024 states that the system has been operational since the end of 2021.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The 2022-2026 plan sets three go-live phases, the first being client registration and appointments across all relevant units.

Not held. The tiers using the system, where the record is entered and the primary clinics using it are not established. Finance is not stated, and nothing dated inside the last twelve months is held.

TCD.short: The ministry signed a partnership for electronic medical records in its hospitals (reported August 2026); no facility is yet shown using one.
TCD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Public Health and Prevention leads the electronic medical record initiative, with HISP Rwanda as technical assistant, HISP Rwanda states. Guinéenews reports that Kouma Academy supplies its Visa Medical record under a model in which the company invests its own funds in the equipment and infrastructure of public hospitals, and has an agreement with the ministry.

Tiers in use. The partnership Guinéenews reported on 13 August 2026 is for the national digitalisation of the country's hospitals with the Visa Medical digital medical record.

Where data is digitised. HISP Rwanda describes the record whose implementation it supports as a patient-centred Dossier Médical Électronique.

Last twelve months. On 15 April 2026 the ministry's Secretary-General chaired a high-level meeting devoted to modernising the patient medical record, and by 13 August 2026 Kouma Academy had signed its partnership with the ministry.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Guinéenews describes the partnership as covering the country's hospitals.

Not held. No electronic medical record is held in use at any facility: no tier, no place of digitisation and no clinic figure. Neither the partnership nor the ministry's initiative carries a deployment, a pilot site, a budget or a timetable.

TGO.short: The World Bank reported in December 2025 that no electronic health record system was in place.
TGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's additional-financing paper of 24 December 2025 states that since October 2025 the health ministry has been responsible for the health and insurance systems layer, including the electronic health record (EHR). The financing pays EUR 866,112.50 on establishment of the system and EUR 173,223 for every 10 contracted facilities with an EHR.

Tiers in use. The paper records "No" at December 2025 for the establishment of an electronic health record system.

Where data is digitised. The Togo Digital 2025 strategy of April 2021 plans a digital and centralised medical record, as something to be developed.

Last twelve months. On 24 December 2025 the World Bank put forward additional financing, a EUR 60.6 million credit and US$11 million in grants, with new conditions for establishing an EHR in facilities contracted under the national health insurance scheme, starting with a pilot.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The paper's results framework gives a baseline of 0 facilities contracted with the national health insurance scheme holding an EHR at December 2025, out of about 335 contracted facilities.

Not held. No source states in terms that patient records are on paper at every tier, and the baseline does not cover facilities outside the insurance scheme. Where records are digitised is not held.

TUN.short: Electronic records are fully used in 50% of university hospitals and 32% of regional hospitals (2025), with pilot sites in one region's primary care.
TUN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. WHO Tunisia stated in April 2024 that the Ministry of Health's Information Technology Centre develops and implements the hospital information management system, with a focus on electronic medical records. The draft National Health Policy of 2019 calls for the generalisation of a single, digitised medical record. The first-line record, which the programme calls the DMI, was developed under Essaha Aziza, a Ministry of Health and European Union programme.

Tiers in use. The World Bank's project document of 2 April 2025 gives the record as fully installed and used in 50 per cent of university hospitals and partially used in the other 50 per cent, and as fully operational in 32 per cent of regional hospitals, partially used in 52 per cent and absent from 16 per cent. In district hospitals it is neither installed nor used.

Where data is digitised. Of primary health care, the same document states that the health system remains largely paper-based and that the DMI pilot faces connectivity and functionality issues.

Last twelve months. The Ministry of Health confirmed on 21 July 2026 that the Sahetna.tn portal, through which citizens are to reach their medical records, had completed technical validation and a cybersecurity audit; it was not yet in service.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Essaha Aziza states that it monitored the DMI's deployment on pilot sites in Nabeul. DH Arab, on the ministry's account at 25 September 2026, has 99 healthcare facilities at various stages of implementing electronic medical records.

Not held. No count of hospitals or of primary clinics using the record is held; the 99 facilities carry no tier and the Nabeul pilot sites no number. The plan is an uncosted draft of 2019, and no domestic budget line for the record is named.

TZA.short: A government system runs in 23.25% of all health facilities (2023 survey); records are not shown to be shared between facilities.
TZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The mid-term review of the Health Sector Strategic Plan V, published in March 2025, states that the Ministry of Health developed and launched Afya eHMS for all regional hospitals and plans to phase out the vendor-dependent Medipro and E-Medical used in zonal and specialised hospitals. It records that the Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024 had run out and its 2025-2030 successor was still being developed.

Tiers in use. The Citizen reported on 1 September 2026 that electronic medical record coverage had reached 100 percent of national, specialised, zonal and regional referral hospitals, and that adoption had expanded across district hospitals, health centres and dispensaries. The mid-term review of March 2025 states that all 28 regional hospitals use Afya eHMS.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's guidelines of May 2019 state that most confidential health data is held in health facilities in paper-based registers.

Last twelve months. The Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health said on 1 October 2025 that the country has an integrated electronic medical records system linking a patient's information from community level through health centres and district hospitals to national level.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The mid-term review, citing the SARA survey of 2023, gives 23.25% of all health facilities using GOT-HoMIS, the government's facility system, against 44.9% of health centres and 10.63% of dispensaries. In March 2025 it states that more than 3,000 primary health care facilities use it as their electronic medical record system.

Not held. Nothing held establishes where the patient record is digitised or whether it can be retrieved at another facility. No financing is stated, no dated event falls in the last twelve months, and no community system is shown exchanging with the EMR.

UGA.short: The ministry's electronic record ran in referral and general hospitals and seven health centres in 2025; records are not shown to be shared.
UGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's guidelines of 18 September 2024 name the ministry as owner of the Electronic Medical Records System. The US-Uganda memorandum signed on 10 December 2025 names eAfya and ClinicMaster as the Government of Uganda's electronic medical records and sets a functional EMR in all facilities down to Health Centre III by 2028. Under it the United States plans US$113,102,289 for data systems over 2026-2030.

Tiers in use. The ministry says that as of 2025 the EMR is in referral and general hospitals and in some health centres. In Kiryandongo district it was in use in September 2026 at the general hospital, Nyakadoti Health Centre III and Mpumwe and Apodorwa Health Centre IIs.

Where data is digitised. The in-charge of Nyakadoti Health Centre III said on 19 September 2026 that patient data must be captured in the EMR at every stage of the visit. A census of all 265 government Health Centre IVs and hospitals, published in October 2025, found 94.3% keeping both paper and digital patient records.

Last twelve months. On 31 March 2026 Makerere University's METS programme handed the UgandaEMR repositories to the Ministry of Health. Health workers told a baraza on 19 September 2026 that the EMR was slowing care in Kiryandongo facilities because of poor connectivity, unstable power and too few computers.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry counts 5 Health Centre IVs and 2 Health Centre IIIs using the EMR as of 2025.

Not held. Nothing held shows a record retrievable at another facility, or what share of primary clinics use the EMR; hospital coverage is disputed between the ministry and a census of government facilities. No domestic budget line for the EMR is held.

ZAF.short: Hospital systems run in five provinces and 308 Western Cape primary facilities use electronic records (August 2025); there is no national count.
ZAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Minister of Health told Parliament on 1 August 2025 that the National Department of Health is developing a single common Electronic Medical Record for primary health care facilities. The department's bid document of March 2026 says it developed the EMR itself and that its Digital Health Unit directs implementation.

Tiers in use. The same reply counts Clinicom in 53 Western Cape hospitals, the eHealth system in 42 KwaZulu-Natal public hospitals and HMS2 in 16 Free State hospitals. It states that Mpumalanga, North West, Limpopo and Northern Cape are not implementing such systems at hospitals.

Where data is digitised. The department describes its EMR, in March 2026, as capturing clinical information at the point of care, verified against the patient's identifier in the Health Patient Registration System.

Last twelve months. In March 2026 the department invited bids to scale up its EMR to all fixed primary health care facilities in eight provinces within 18 months. The Free State Department of Health won the Public Sector Digital Innovator Award for deploying its primary health care EMR, SAnews reported in May 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Minister's reply states that the National EMR beta ran in 36 primary health care facilities between 22 October 2024 and 13 February 2025 and that Western Cape's Primary Health Care Information System is implemented in 308. It counts 3,333 primary health care facilities reporting to the 2024/25 Ideal Clinic Assessment.

Not held. No count of primary facilities using the national EMR in 2026 is held, and no total of hospitals against which the provincial counts can be set. Nothing held shows a record retrieved at another facility, and no funding source is named.

ZMB.short: An electronic record system was in use at 877 of 3,540 health facilities of all kinds (April 2025); the share of primary clinics is unknown.
ZMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Global Fund's case study of April 2025 states that the Ministry of Health developed SmartCare and describes it as co-financed by the Global Fund. SMART Zambia's national coordinator said on 7 July 2026 that government aims at full national coverage of SmartCare Pro.

Tiers in use. SmartCare 2.0 Hospital Edition went live as a pilot at Ndola Teaching Hospital on 27 April 2026. Interviews of May and June 2019 found some larger health centres and hospitals collecting data in the electronic health record, in select districts.

Where data is digitised. The programme managers' presentation of March 2025 describes SmartCare Pro as capturing the patient encounter at facility level, on a central server that identifies each client uniquely and tracks patients between facilities. The implementers described in January 2026 a nurse at a rural clinic in Kafulafuta identifying a patient by fingerprint to reach his record.

Last twelve months. ITWeb Africa reported on 16 July 2026 that SmartCare Pro and SmartCare 2.0 will be migrated to the government-owned GovLink network, with three Copperbelt hospitals connected first.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Global Fund states that SmartCare Pro is in use at 877 health facilities, against 3,540 health facilities in Zambia, at April 2025. The March 2025 presentation puts SmartCare Legacy and SmartCare Plus together in approximately 1,800 healthcare facilities. SMART Zambia's national coordinator said on 7 July 2026 that SmartCare Pro has been deployed in approximately 80% of health facilities nationwide.

Not held. No count or share of primary clinics using SmartCare is held: every figure counts health facilities of all kinds, and the 80% is of deployment, with no numerator or denominator. Use at the primary tier rests on 2019 interviews and one rural clinic, and nothing held shows a record retrieved at a second facility in practice.

ZWE.short: An electronic record system ran in 1,254 health facilities of all types in August 2025, out of 1,900 planned; shared records are not shown.
ZWE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Global Fund said in August 2025 that the Government of Zimbabwe has been developing a national EMR system since February 2015, culminating in Impilo, for use in public health facilities. The ministry's National Health Strategy 2021-2025 commits to supporting the deployment of what it calls the electronic health record (Impilo) system. The Global Fund has put over US$43.1 million into digital health in Zimbabwe since 2014, US$9.85 million of it in the 2024-2026 grant cycle.

Tiers in use. The Permanent Secretary for Health and Child Care told The Sunday Mail on 17 November 2024 that the facilities with Impilo are spread across provinces and districts and include clinics, hospitals and other health centres.

Where data is digitised. A 2025 abstract on the DHIS2 community site states that Impilo captures real-time clinical and administrative data for services including HIV testing, antiretroviral therapy and maternal and child health, stored in centralised repositories and a national data warehouse.

Last twelve months. The Herald on 23 September 2026 described Impilo as the Ministry of Health's own electronic health records platform.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Global Fund reports 1,254 health facilities implementing Impilo as of August 2025, with deployment planned for all 1,900 health facilities. The Permanent Secretary put deployment at 1,178 health facilities on 17 November 2024. The Matabeleland South provincial health team reported 110 of the province's 153 health facilities (71.9%) with Impilo fully functional in May 2025.

Not held. Nothing held says an Impilo record can be retrieved at another facility. The counts are of facilities of every type where Impilo is deployed, not of primary clinics entering records, and no strategy current at 30 September 2026 is held.

AGO.short: In 2026 counters in municipal administrations work in a national database, in the 11 municipalities of one province; the national count is not known.
AGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. A presidential order reported on 8 June 2026 created an interministerial commission, coordinated by the Minister of State and head of the Casa Civil, to reinforce the network of Balcões Únicos de Atendimento ao Público (BUAP), as the Government names its public service counters, and charged it with the network's power, computing equipment, communication systems and connectivity. The Ministry of Territorial Administration runs a national programme of V/SAT satellite antennas for commune seats.

What the office does over it. Since 15 June 2026 adult citizens confirm their electoral data at counters installed in municipal and commune administrations, feeding the national database of adult citizens. In Zaire province more than 24,000 adults updated their data at the counters between 15 July and 14 August 2026.

How the office is connected. The ministry's antennas are to guarantee communications and internet at commune seats so that the counters there can work, and ten Zaire commune seats with no UNITEL network were to get them in the days after 14 August 2026.

Last twelve months. The data update began on 15 June 2026 with 254 counters in a first phase and 634 intended. The Cubango provincial government approved on 18 December 2025 a project that provides for internet access in all its municipal administrations, to start in January 2026.

Local governments connected. Twelve counters were working in the 11 municipalities of Zaire province on 14 August 2026, on the provincial director's word.

Not held. No source held says how the counters at municipal seats are connected, or how many municipalities nationally have a working counter. The finance of the counter network is not stated.

BDI.short: A 2021 strategy plans fibre to the communes and one commune's connection was announced in 2024; whether any commune office is connected is not known.
BDI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The sector strategy for the National Development Plan 2018-2027, issued by the Ministry of Communication, Information Technologies and Media in February 2021, names the extension of the government's fibre-optic interconnection to the communes under its e-government project. In Rumonge commune the routers and other equipment for the civil registry service's connection are to come from the local NGO FVS-Amade under a one-year project, its programme officer said on 19 July 2024, and workshop participants said the commune could not keep digital registration going once that support ends.

What the office does over it. The connection announced for Rumonge is for the commune's civil registry service, at the commune seat and in its zones.

How the office is connected. FVS-Amade said on 19 July 2024 that it will give Rumonge's civil registry service computers, tablets, solar panels and routers to ease its connection.

Last twelve months. On 18 July 2026 the interior ministry's Director General for territorial administration said that many civil registration centres have no reliable internet connection for digital services and are poorly equipped with computers.

Local governments connected. The strategy of February 2021 states that about a hundred public institutions are interconnected by a fibre-optic link and that the project needs to be extended to the communes not yet connected. One commune, Rumonge, was named for a connection on 19 July 2024.

Not held. No source held reports a commune office's connection in use, says whether Rumonge's routers were delivered, or counts the communes connected. No change in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is on record.

BEN.short: Twelve more communes' town halls joined the state's administration network in 2024, of 77 communes; the total connected is not known.
BEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Government Action Programme 2021-2026 schedules the connection of communes to the administration's network for 2023-2026, under the Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalisation, and costs its local-government digital project at FCFA 21 billion, FCFA 7 billion of it from the national budget. The finance ministry's 2025 report allocates EUR 6.43 million of the 2021 sovereign Eurobond to digitalising the administration.

What the office does over it. The national land platform, which Benin calls e-Foncier Bénin, has been operational since 1 January 2025 with the participation of town halls, and a parcel is sold at the mairie with every operation done directly in the platform (March 2026).

How the office is connected. Town halls use the services of the Réseau National de l'Administration, the state's own network (2024). The 2021 programme reported a network dedicated to the public administration interconnecting 187 decentralised sites, town halls among the kinds of office it lists.

Last twelve months. The state agency ASIN presented at Bantè's town hall the connecting of the mairie to the network, reported on 18 July 2026. On 11 September 2026 a connection failure in several of Cotonou's arrondissement offices stopped the registering of taxi-duty payments for the day.

Local governments connected. The finance ministry counts 12 new town halls using the network's services in 2024, in a country of 77 communes. KfW reported on 31 May 2023 that 187 authorities were on the network and that connecting all municipalities was the next step.

Not held. No cumulative total of town halls on the state's network is published, and the 2024 count names no system their staff work in over it. Whether the mairies working in the land platform do so over that network is not stated.

BFA.short: Town halls are on the state's network and 78 civil status centres were networked in 2025; the share of the 351 communes is not known.
BFA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The government network, RESINA, is built and run by ANPTIC, a state establishment under the ministry of the digital economy, and the State financed its reinforcement and extension with FCFA 346.2 million in 2020. The national civil status strategy for 2023-2027, steered by the territorial administration ministry, counts the networking of principal civil status centres among its 2025 results.

What the office does over it. ANPTIC says the connection gives interconnected structures, local governments' buildings among them, access to the government intranet's computing resources, to email and to the web (January 2024).

How the office is connected. ANPTIC lists the interconnection of local governments' buildings to RESINA, with internet access at no monthly fee over WiMAX or LTE, microwave or fibre (January 2024). In 2020 its regional antennas gave the Dédougou town hall a local network and RESINA access and connected sites of the Ouagadougou town hall by fibre.

Last twelve months. The strategy's results for 2025, validated on 25 June 2026, report 78 principal civil status centres networked and the declaration software deployed in 30 principal and 140 secondary centres; the ministry names insufficient financing and too few qualified staff as brakes.

Local governments connected. The territorial administration ministry gives 78 principal civil status centres networked in 2025. ANPTIC's report for 2020 names five town halls on RESINA or being put on it: Dédougou, Fada N'Gourma, Tenkodogo, Manga and Ouagadougou.

Not held. No share of the 351 communes' town halls connected is published: the 78 centres networked in 2025 are a count with no total. Nothing held says commune staff work in a national system over the connection, or how the connection has been financed since 2020.

BWA.short: Four councils had partnerships to deploy office Wi-Fi in 2022/23; whether any council office's connection is in use is not known.
BWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The premises Wi-Fi for council centres is recorded as partnerships between BoFiNet and four local authorities, in the company's annual report for financial year 2022/23.

What the office does over it. District officials uploaded beneficiary data to the national social registry every month as at May 2021, the World Bank says; its review names the registry the Single Social Registry.

How the office is connected. By the end of financial year 2022/23 BoFiNet had partnered with four local authorities for the deployment of premises Wi-Fi in their Rural Administration Centres.

Last twelve months. The four deployment partnerships stood at the end of financial year 2022/23, in March 2023.

Local governments connected. The four are Serowe and Mahalapye District Councils and Bobirwa and Boteti Sub District Councils, as BoFiNet lists them for 2022/23. The local government ministry ran the social registry pilot in four districts in 2019 and 2020, Gaborone, Kweneng, Kgatleng and South East, and had uploaded beneficiary data in six districts by May 2021, the World Bank says.

Not held. No source states that a council's own office has a connection in use, or gives the total of councils. Nothing dated after March 2023 is held on the councils' connection, nor who plans and pays for it.

CAF.short: A fund meant to bring broadband to town halls was still being set up in April 2026; how many communes are connected is not known.
CAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The universal service fund (Fonds du service universel) is supervised and managed by the Comité de développement des communications électroniques, a body set by law, with the regulator ARCEP selecting the operators it pays. It is fed mainly by a levy of 2% of telecom operators' turnover of the previous year. ARCEP listed finishing the fund's set-up among its priorities for 2026 when it presented a draft budget of 6.2 billion FCFA on 15 April 2026, Agence Ecofin reports.

What the office does over it. The fund's framework provides for broadband internet access in mairies.

How the office is connected. The fund was not yet in operation on 15 April 2026.

Last twelve months. The committee that manages the fund began its activities in July 2025, and on 15 April 2026 ARCEP said the fund's effective set-up was planned for 2026.

Local governments connected. Mairies are in the fund's scope alongside schools, health centres, libraries and post offices, under law 18.002 of 17 January 2018 and a decree of February 2019.

Not held. No source states that any mairie's office is connected, how, or what its staff do over a connection, and no count or share of communes is held. There is no dated statement that local government offices have no connection of their own.

CIV.short: A loan-financed programme to connect the communes' town halls was ratified in February 2026; how many are connected is not known.
CIV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalization implements phase 1 of PADCI, with the Republic as borrower. The project runs from 2025 to 2030 and carries US$45 million for broadband to targeted public institutions, town halls among them, in Abidjan, Yamoussoukro and twelve regions. In September 2025 a separate project for the connectivity of town halls was funded by the European Union and implemented by CIVIPOL.

What the office does over it. ONECI's civil-status project lead said on 11 August 2026 that birth data entered by health staff on new digital terminals is transmitted in real time to the civil-status office, notably the mairies or sous-préfectures.

How the office is connected. The digital ministry's plan for PADCI, dated May 2025, targets public facilities, mairies among them, that have electricity but no internet, and gives the government's ambition as broadband for all mairies.

Last twelve months. Côte d'Ivoire and IDA concluded the loan agreement for PADCI phase 1 on 17 October 2025. On 4 February 2026 the Council of Ministers ratified the loan of 84,356,070,200 FCFA by decree.

Local governments connected. The World Bank's appraisal document of 18 September 2025 says the project aims to connect more than 1,300 schools, hospitals, courts and municipalities to high-speed internet, phase 1 covering selected regions and phase 2 the country. The ministry's plan sets the connection of mairies for 2025 to 2030.

Not held. No source states a town hall connected and in use, and none gives a count or share of town halls connected or to be connected. The civil-status data sent to the mairies is not described as arriving over a connection of the mairie's own.

CMR.short: Two commune offices in the East Region had an internet connection in August 2026; how many of the 360 communes are connected is not known.
CMR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. On 2 June 2026 the government presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion programme over three years to improve connectivity and equip decentralised local authorities, and was still seeking its financing from partners. The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications is contracting authority for PATNUC, whose connectivity for local authorities is paid from a World Bank loan of US$100 million. In August 2026 the commune of Bertoua 1er had a budget line of its own for maintenance and the internet connection.

What the office does over it. APC's policy brief of 2023 says the pilot networks at Mayo-Oulo and Bibemi give the connected sites, the two town halls among them, internet access and offline access to the GOON platform of local content.

How the office is connected. UNDP Cameroon reported in August 2026 that Bertoua 1er budgets for the internet connection of its digitised civil status service. The town halls of Mayo-Oulo and Bibemi were each fitted with a Wi-Fi access point on a long-distance Wi-Fi link, by APC's brief of 2023.

Last twelve months. On 3 October 2025 the posts ministry sought a consultant for a 120-day needs assessment under component 2 of PATNUC. DIGI-CoR went to funders in Yaoundé on 2 June 2026.

Local governments connected. UNDP Cameroon's monitoring of six East Region sites in August 2026 states an internet connection at two commune offices: Bétaré-Oya, where it is available but unstable, and Bertoua 1er. Cameroon has 360 communes and 14 urban communities.

Not held. No share or total of communes connected is published; the two offices are those one region's monitoring names. Who pays for the connection at Bétaré-Oya, what staff do over the connection, and whether any commune office works in a national system held elsewhere are not stated.

COD.short: In March 2026 one province handed satellite internet kits to 45 chiefdoms and sectors; whether any office works over them is not known.
COD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The provider is a provincial government: the governor of Haut-Uélé handed the kits to the heads of the province's decentralised territorial entities at Isiro on 17 March 2026.

What the office does over it. The kits are for the heads of the entities to send security alerts to the provincial capital in real time, in the governor's words.

How the office is connected. By satellite: the entities were given Starlink internet kits, in a province where the lack of a telecom network remains a problem.

Last twelve months. The handover of 17 March 2026 followed the recommendations of the 2025 forum on security governance.

Local governments connected. 45 chiefdoms and sectors of Haut-Uélé received kits on 17 March 2026, beside 6 territories and the security services, according to the provincial information note.

Not held. No source says any chiefdom, sector or commune office is working over a connection: the kits in Haut-Uélé are reported handed over, not installed or in use, and who pays the subscription is not stated. The 45 comes with no total of entities, and no plan naming the connection of local governments or budget line is on record.

COG.short: In February 2026 a World Bank-funded project was asked to extend internet access to town halls; how many communes are connected is not known.
COG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Internet access for town halls falls under the Projet d'accélération de la transformation numérique (Patn), which the World Bank finances for US$100 million and whose 2026 work plan and budget was adopted at XAF 21.872 billion on 26 February 2026, according to ACI. The Bank's appraisal of May 2022 expects shared connectivity to be supplied to decentralised local authorities.

What the office does over it. The access is meant to let public administrations interconnect with the state's digital platforms.

How the office is connected. The project is to provide internet access within the public administrations themselves, town halls included.

Last twelve months. At its fifth session on 26 February 2026 the Patn steering committee recommended continuing and intensifying the extension of internet access and approved reallocating funds towards the connectivity component.

Local governments connected. Town halls are named with ministries and hospitals among the administrations to be given access. The May 2022 appraisal planned fibre for 22 ministries, departments and agencies in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, national and local government service providers alike.

Not held. No source says any town hall is connected: no count, share or place is given, and no use over a connection is named. Who owns the connection is not held within the last three years.

COM.short: Only civil-status and central systems are held, the latest from 2026; whether the communes' offices are connected is not known, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not held. Nothing held states whether the office of any of the 54 communes is connected. No published count of connected communes was found.

CPV.short: Municipal councils worked in national systems in 2025, 21 of 22 supplied with state digital services; how many offices are connected is not known.
CPV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. NOSi, a public enterprise, supplies the municipal councils with what it calls Local Digital Governance services, under a contract signed with each council, on its communiqué of 6 October 2025. The councils pay it current invoices under those agreements. Its plan for 2019-2022 budgeted ECV 25,000,000 for the state's private network.

What the office does over it. The social development ministry, on a page published in September 2018, says registration in the Cadastro Social Único, a national system, is done locally by the municipal councils. Until 17 December 2025 the registry's declaration was issued and printed at the councils. Councils on Sal, Boa Vista, Maio and rural São Vicente use the shared land platform SIGTP, on Ministry of Finance terms of reference published in March 2022.

How the office is connected. NOSi's strategic plan of March 2020 lists the municipal councils' local area networks among those served by basic access to the state's private network, which it calls the Rede Tecnológica Privativa do Estado.

Last twelve months. By 6 October 2025 NOSi's services to the Mosteiros council were not in regular supply, over unpaid invoices. The association of municipalities said it was indignant at the suspension of services, and NOSi reported a very low payment rate across the councils.

Local governments connected. NOSi says 21 of the 22 municipalities, all but Mosteiros, were receiving its services regularly on 6 October 2025.

Not held. No share of councils connected: the 21 of 22 are councils supplied with NOSi's services, and that source does not say how their offices are connected. The connection rests on one plan of March 2020 that gives no count of councils, and no plan covering 2026 is held.

DJI.short: In 2024 Djibouti city's three communes recorded civil status in the city's system; connection of local governments outside the capital is not known.
DJI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The system the commune centres work in belongs to the city: the PROGOUV terms of reference of February 2024 describe Djibouti city's computerised civil-status system, which the city calls SIGEC, with its data held on a central server in a room of the town hall.

What the office does over it. At February 2024 the civil-status centres of Djibouti city's three communes recorded civil-status events in SIGEC, as did five maternity antennas.

How the office is connected. The records the commune centres enter sit on a central server at the town hall, as the terms of reference of February 2024 describe it.

Last twelve months. In February 2024 three commune centres and five antennas in health facilities were working in SIGEC.

Local governments connected. Three commune civil-status centres worked in SIGEC at February 2024, one in each of Balbala, Ras Dika and Boulaos, the three communes of Djibouti city. All three are in the capital.

Not held. No source held states how the commune civil-status centres are connected or who provides and pays for the link, and none places a local government office outside Djibouti city on a connection. No national total of local governments is held, nor anything on governance or on the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

DZA.short: All 1,541 communes worked in national systems over the interior ministry's network in 2019; a later count and the rural share are not known.
DZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The network linking the communes to the national civil-status database is the interior ministry's own, on its presentation of June 2019. It was on the ministry's directives that municipal services moved onto the national vehicle-registration platform on 5 April 2026. The commune of Bouira bears its own annual internet subscription, the Court of Accounts found in September 2023.

What the office does over it. Communes and their annexes issue birth, marriage and death acts from any commune in the country, from commune databases linked to a national one (June 2019). Since 5 April 2026 municipal services work in the national vehicle-registration system, a centralised platform that replaced local applications. In September 2023 Bouira used 55 applications, 41 of them the ministry's.

How the office is connected. The ministry's architecture slide of June 2019 shows commune, wilaya and ministry levels linked over its own network, which it labels "Réseau MICL". Bouira has no intranet and links its floors to the internet by Wi-Fi, the Court of Accounts found in September 2023.

Last twelve months. On 5 April 2026 municipal services began the third phase of generalising the national vehicle-registration system, ending manual and local procedures.

Local governments connected. The interior ministry's presentation of June 2019 shows 1,541 commune databases on the civil-status network: 1,541 of 1,541 communes, on its own account. The Court of Accounts says the ministry's human-resources system was placed at all communes and wilayas, in an audit covering 2019 to 2024.

Not held. No count of communes connected is held after the interior ministry's of June 2019, and no source held gives a rural share. No current plan with a stated period is held, and who pays for a commune's link is stated for one commune only.

EGY.short: In 2024 one governorate was the pilot for linking districts and local units; whether any local unit office is connected is not known.
EGY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Egypt's project to automate local administration and governorate headquarters, as its minister of communications named it on 15 January 2024, is carried out by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology with the Ministry of Local Development and the governors. It sits within the state's institutional digital transformation project.

What the office does over it. The project is to start at governorate headquarters, move to governorate capitals and districts, and end with local units.

How the office is connected. The minister expected the Minya governorate headquarters to be linked electronically to the governorate's districts and local units during 2024.

Last twelve months. The minister described the project and named its pilot on 15 January 2024.

Local governments connected. Minya was chosen as the pilot for the first digital governorate headquarters, with the rest of local administration to follow it.

Not held. Whether any governorate headquarters, district or local unit office is connected or works over a connection, and whether the Minya link expected for 2024 was made. What the offices would do over it, the kind of connection, a plan, a funder and any event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

ERI.short: Whether any sub-zoba administration office is connected is not known as at 2026, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not held. Whether any sub-zoba administration has a connection. What is held concerns the zoba population registers and central systems.

ETH.short: Addis Ababa piloted a connection from the centre to its woredas in 2025; whether any woreda office outside the capital is connected is not known.
ETH.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Addis Ababa City Administration runs the one-stop service centres it calls Addis Mesob and their digital system, on its director general's report of July 2026. The city's civil registration and residency system was launched by the city administration for its own agency and built by the state's Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute in December 2025.

What the office does over it. Over the Addis Ababa connectivity, family registration, vital events registration, resident services and verification are carried out through a digital system built with locally developed applications, a government statement published on 22 December 2025 says. Outside the capital, the World Bank said in October 2025 that 444 of the safety net programme's 492 woredas use its management information system for programme tracking, which is the programme's own system and not the woreda administration's.

How the office is connected. In Addis Ababa connectivity has been created from the central level down to the woreda level for civil registration and citizenship services, the deputy director general of the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute said in the statement of 22 December 2025.

Last twelve months. Addis Ababa's mayor launched the Integrated Civil Registration and Residency Service Technology on 5 December 2025 and said implementation would start in 50 of the city's woredas on 8 December 2025.

Local governments connected. The central-to-woreda connectivity is a major pilot, in Addis Ababa only, on the statement of 22 December 2025.

Not held. No woreda office outside Addis Ababa is put on a connection provided to it, and no count of woredas connected or total of woredas is given. No plan naming the connection of woredas and no source of finance for it is stated.

GAB.short: One commune's town hall, at Oyem, was on the state administration network in 2026; how many of the communes are connected is not known.
GAB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Réseau de l'Administration Gabonaise, the RAG, is a public network dedicated to the administrations and controlled by the State, activated at Oyem by ANINF, the State's operational arm for public digital infrastructure, Gabon Review reported on 1 April 2026.

What the office does over it. The connection at Oyem improves the working conditions of the public services and prepares the progressive integration of new digital uses in the administrations on it, on Gabon Review's account of April 2026.

How the office is connected. The Mairie Centrale d'Oyem is among the administrations of the town already on the RAG, a fibre-optic network that ANINF has brought into service there, as reported on 1 April 2026.

Last twelve months. The RAG fibre at Oyem, installed in 2010 and inactive since, has been brought into service by ANINF, Gabon Review reported on 1 April 2026.

Local governments connected. One town hall is named on the network, the Mairie Centrale d'Oyem in Woleu-Ntem, beside the town's police station and courthouse, with activation to continue to other administrations of the locality and then to other public entities, as at April 2026.

Not held. No total of communes connected or to be connected is given, and no system the town hall's staff work in is named. No plan and no source of finance is stated, and the activation at Oyem is not dated.

GHA.short: The government network connected all 274 planned sites of metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies in 2024; how many of the 261 assemblies is not known.
GHA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation tendered the government network it calls eGovNet in September 2021, awarded it to AirtelTigo and Ascend Digital Solutions in September 2022 and signed a 10-year contract in December 2022. On 3 September 2026 the Head of the Local Government Service presented a programme his office calls LITISIP to give the 261 metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies a secure digital backbone.

What the office does over it. The minister said in February 2024 that the network gives the connected agencies, the assemblies among them, faster communication and access to government shared services. The Ministry of Finance's budget guidelines of 29 August 2025 carry instructions to the assemblies with a part on GIFMIS, the national financial management system.

How the office is connected. The minister said in February 2024 that the network connects government agencies, the assemblies included, by fibre backbone, last-mile fibre and microwave links with satellite backup, on a 10-year indefeasible right of use. At a signing reported on 3 September 2026 the Head of the Local Government Service described the state the Service is moving from as "disconnected offices".

Last twelve months. The Local Government Service signed a memorandum of understanding with Celltel Networks, reported on 3 September 2026, with improved connectivity of local government offices among its expected results.

Local governments connected. The minister's table of February 2024 gives the assemblies 274 of 274 planned sites connected, within 950 of 951 government sites.

Not held. How many of the 261 assemblies the 274 connected sites cover, and how many assembly offices are without a connection in 2026. What LITISIP costs, who pays for it and when it is due, and which systems assembly staff work in over the network.

GIN.short: Commune registry staff worked in a national civil-registration system in 2026, with rural offices on paper; how many communes are connected is not known.
GIN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Enabel, the Belgian development agency, issued the tender of 27 July 2022 for the internet connection of 10 pilot communes, the notice citing Belgium's bilateral portfolio of EUR 45 million for 2019 to 2023.

What the office does over it. The delegated civil-registry officer of Ratoma commune said, as reported on 2 September 2026, that his office goes on registering births in the digital civil-registration system, which runs from a data centre held elsewhere. Enabel's final evaluation, from fieldwork in April 2026, says civil-status officers and data-entry agents at civil registry centres work in the national civil register's central database, which it calls E-RENEC, with paper still in use in parallel. A policy brief of November 2025 says weak connectivity, high data costs and low digital literacy force rural municipal offices onto manual reporting and paper records.

How the office is connected. That tender was for a service contract for the internet connection of 10 communes, closing on 17 August 2022.

Last twelve months. The relocation of the system's data centre from the Maison centrale disrupted the service to commune offices, on top of a stockout of secure paper lasting about two weeks, as reported on 2 September 2026.

Local governments connected. The tender of 2022 names the 10 pilot communes: the 5 of Conakry, Kassa, Coyah, Kindia, Mamou and Tolo. The evaluation describes E-RENEC as the product of a pilot project and recommends a maturity diagnosis before any national extension.

Not held. Whether the internet connection tendered for the 10 pilot communes in 2022 was delivered, how commune offices are connected today, and how many communes work in the civil-registration system. Who owns and pays for the connection since 2022, and how many rural offices are without one.

GMB.short: All councils had the government's finance system by late 2024 and most used it; capped because no current plan or budget line is known.
GMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The rollout of IFMIS, the government's Integrated Financial Management Information System, to the councils is a reform of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs, with the system run by the Accountant General's Department. In 2024 it was the first component of the local government pillar of the Public Financial Management Strategy 2021-2025. The ministry's report for the second and third quarters of 2025 says the government lacks funds for a localised IFMIS.

What the office does over it. Most councils were actively using IFMIS in 2024, on the ministry's report. In the second and third quarters of 2025 Kuntaur Area Council was posting live in it and Basse Area Council used it for its accounting.

How the office is connected. By late 2024 Janjanbureh and Kuntaur area councils had working internet connections reaching most of their offices and Banjul City Council had a 100 Mbps connection, the ministry reported. In the second and third quarters of 2025 internet speed and connectivity remained problems at Brikama Area Council.

Last twelve months. The ministry's report for the second and third quarters of 2025 has Kuntaur extending internet across its offices and Brikama installing IFMIS for all its users.

Local governments connected. IFMIS had been implemented in all Local Government Area Councils by the end of 2024, on the ministry's report, which names eight councils. Its report for the second and third quarters of 2025 describes IFMIS in use or being installed at four of them.

Not held. No share of councils connected is held after 2024, no rural share, and no plan covering 2026 or domestic budget line for the councils' connections. Whether IFMIS works at Kanifing is not held: its mayor said in August 2026 that it had not for two years, and the Accountant General's Department disputes that.

GNB.short: No sector administration, nor the Bissau municipal chamber, is known to have an office connection in 2026, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not held. Nothing held puts a sector administration or the Bissau municipal chamber on a connection. No local elections have been held, and the documents found concern the national backbone.

GNQ.short: In 2024 the government's network did not reach local government offices, which worked largely on manual systems; whether any has another connection is not known.
GNQ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's digital economy diagnostic of 2024 describes a central network of the government, partly hosted by CNIAPGE. It puts manual working at the local level down to a want of funds and adequate infrastructure.

What the office does over it. The diagnostic states that many ministries at the centre operate on manual systems, and that this is more pronounced at the local level. Data pass between ministries by hand, USB drive or e-mail.

How the office is connected. In 2024 the World Bank stated that the government's central network does not extend to local government branches.

Last twelve months. On 18 December 2025 Gabon's Council of Ministers approved an agreement to interconnect the fibre-optic networks of Gabon and Equatorial Guinea, which are the two countries' national networks.

Local governments connected. The World Bank's statement of 2024 is about local government branches as a whole, which the central network does not reach.

Not held. Whether a local government office holds any connection other than the government's central network, and how many local governments there are to connect. No owner, plan or finance for connecting them, and no event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

KEN.short: All 47 counties were on the government network by 2017 and work in national systems; how many county offices are connected is not known.
KEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy presents the County Connectivity Project as its own, with two further phases started in 2022. The ICT Authority's plan for 2024 to 2027 states that county governments have not prioritised ICT investment and rely on national government initiatives for their connectivity.

What the office does over it. The Controller of Budget's review of the year to 30 June 2026, as the Daily Nation reports it, has county governments processing payroll in the national Human Resource Information System, which Kenya calls HRIS-Ke, with at least Sh8.3 billion in salaries still paid by manual payroll outside it. The National Treasury's draft payment policy of August 2026 says the Central Bank rolled out internet banking for county governments.

How the office is connected. The ministry states that the counties were connected by secure connections into the national private governmental voice and data network, which it calls NOFBI, the last of them by 2017.

Last twelve months. On 25 August 2026 the National Treasury's Cabinet Secretary announced that all 47 county governments must finish integrating the national electronic procurement platform with its financial management system by 30 September 2026. In the year to June 2026 counties cited connectivity challenges among their reasons for manual payroll.

Local governments connected. The ministry states that Phase I, in 2012 and 2013, connected 28 counties and Nairobi, and Phase 2, completed in 2017, the remaining 18 of the 47 it names.

Not held. The share of county government offices connected: the ministry's 47 of 47 counts counties, and nothing since 2017 gives a figure. Where the staff working in the national systems sit, how those offices are connected, and any plan, finance or connection event dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

LBR.short: A 2019 policy targeted internet access at every county Superintendent office; whether any is connected is not known, so no stage is set.
LBR.summary: Not held. Whether any county Superintendent office is connected, how, what it does over the connection and how many are. The one target on record, internet access at every Superintendent office, belongs to the national ICT policy for 2019-2024, and no dated statement that the offices lack a connection is held.

LBY.short: Three municipalities' offices had unreliable internet access in a 2021 study; how many of Libya's municipalities are connected is not known.
LBY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Local Government's digital transformation project director said on 2 November 2023 that official e-mail accounts would be created for the heads of administrative units in the municipalities, inside the ministry's electronic correspondence system, to replace paper correspondence. The system is the ministry's own, run under its digital transformation project.

What the office does over it. In the three local authorities studied by Wynn, Bakeer and Forti, published in 2021, the information systems are isolated in-house or third-party systems on departmental networks, and data is exchanged on paper. Sabratha's finance department uses online services occasionally, to display and update information on the authority's website.

How the office is connected. The study finds internet access at the authorities' offices that is slow, often disconnected or not always available. Sabratha's finance department has fifteen networked computers and an internet connection that is often disconnected, and in Rujban the internet is normally unavailable in community services and unreliable in human resources.

Last twelve months. On 2 November 2023 the e-mail accounts for municipal units were announced and not yet in use.

Local governments connected. The 2021 study covers three local authorities, Misurata, Sabratha and Rujban, by questionnaire and interviews with eighteen officials, and concludes for the three that access to the internet was not always available.

Not held. No total or share of Libya's municipalities with a connected office is held, nor who provides or pays for the offices' internet. The period and the finance of the ministry's strategy are not stated, the newest fact on the offices' connection is of 2021, and nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held.

LSO.short: Two community councils had internet installed under a pilot by 2019; whether any connection has gone beyond the pilot is not known.
LSO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The e-Government Project that built and connected two community council buildings is under the Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology, which handed them to the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftainship Affairs on 31 July 2019. The project is financially supported by the African Development Bank.

What the office does over it. The 31 July 2019 handover report states that the two buildings have the Internet installed. In January 2018 the secretary of Tenesolo Community Council said e-government would connect the office to internet access and to a data bank in Mohale's Hoek. In September 2025 the civil registration manager for Qacha's Nek said certificate services decentralised to councils fail without transport to carry applications to and from the district office.

How the office is connected. The Minister said on 31 July 2019 that the two buildings handed over under his ministry's project have been installed with the Internet. In January 2018 the head of the national web e-portal said council connections will use the Lesotho government data network.

Last twelve months. On 17 June 2024 the communications ministry's Principal Secretary said its plan is to roll out its 74 digital services by also connecting Community Councils.

Local governments connected. Two community councils, Dinizulu in Thaba-Tseka and Kubake in Maseru district, had the Internet installed by 31 July 2019 under the e-Government Pilot Project begun in 2014. In January 2018 the Minister said the plan is to assist in connecting all the councils.

Not held. Whether any community council beyond the two pilot ones is connected, and how many councils there are in all. What system council staff work in over the connection, and any plan period or financing since 2019.

MAR.short: A revenue system was deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities of all tiers by 2020; how commune offices are connected is not known.
MAR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Interior Ministry's directorate for local governments is responsible for the programme under which GIR-CT, Rokhas, the civil registry system and Chikaya were rolled out to participating municipalities.
